💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sell on Fiverr if your service can be packaged at a set price, like logo design or voiceovers, because buyers search for it and order without a pitch from you.
  • Recent findings suggest that fiverr is a freelance marketplace where you sell your skills as packaged services, called gigs, at prices you set.
  • Freelancers with a service they can package and price up front, such as logo design, editing, or voiceovers, get a storefront that buyers already search, and that’s worth the 20% cut.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sell on Fiverr if your service can be packaged at a set price, like logo design or voiceovers, because buyers search for it and order without a pitch from you. Fiverr keeps 20% of every order, tips included, so build that cut into each package’s price.

Recent findings suggest that fiverr is a freelance marketplace where you sell your skills as packaged services, called gigs, at prices you set. On a $100 order, you keep $80 after Fiverr’s 20% cut and pay no Fiverr fee to withdraw it to PayPal, so price a package at $125 to net $100.

Freelancers with a service they can package and price up front, such as logo design, editing, or voiceovers, get a storefront that buyers already search, and that’s worth the 20% cut. A consultant whose work needs a custom quote does better on Upwork, where freelancers send proposals to the jobs clients post.

Take out a Navy Federal home equity loan or line if you’re a member who needs to borrow most of your equity, since Navy Federal pays the closing costs and lends up to all of it. With a top credit score and plenty of equity, get a quote from a bank too before you choose.

Navy Federal Credit Union pays the closing costs on its fixed-rate home equity loan and home equity line of credit (HELOC), and charges no application or origination fee, but only members can borrow. Membership is open to service members, veterans, Defense Department civilians, and their family and household members.

Navy Federal fits members who need to borrow most of their equity or want a line with no annual fee to keep for years. Anyone who can’t join needs another lender, and a member with a 730-plus credit score wanting a $50,000-plus line, with total borrowing at 60% of the home’s value or less, should get a quote from U.S. Bank where it lends.

#148305. How to Navigate the Tariff Circus

📅 13 Jun 2025 • ⏱️ 12m • 📚 Deep Dive (2444 w)

How to Navigate the Tariff Circus

📅 13 Jun 2025 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2444 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mrmoneymustache

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that quite accidentally, it looks like we timed our last talk about the stock market pretty darned well.
  • And although stock market volatility doesn’t always come with an easily labeled explanation, this time the reason seems pretty clear: it’s the Tariffs.
  • As our financial world has been whipped around like a circus tent in a hurricane for the last several months, almost everyone who has a stake in this country has been wondering what to make of it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that quite accidentally, it looks like we timed our last talk about the stock market pretty darned well. Back in February 2025, the market put the perfect cap on a multi year climb before stepping onto the wild roller coaster we’re currently riding. Since then it has seen some of the steepest drops and recoveries in history, losing a full 20% of its value at the bottom while somehow managing to end up right back near the peak as I’m writing this.

And although stock market volatility doesn’t always come with an easily labeled explanation, this time the reason seems pretty clear: it’s the Tariffs.

As our financial world has been whipped around like a circus tent in a hurricane for the last several months, almost everyone who has a stake in this country has been wondering what to make of it.

As I write this, we still don’t know the outcome of the worldwide tariff and trade battle that our unpredictable government has unleashed upon the world. But we’re already seeing the results: businesses are bracing for massive changes, currencies and interest rates are reacting, and regular investors like you and me are wondering what the future holds for our early retirement funds. Surveying my own group of friends, the reactions span the whole range of emotions from “this is a giant Nothingburger” to “we’re all totally screwed.”.

Sources indicate that so what’s the real answer? To get closer to that, we should start with the most basic question of:.

A tariff is just a sales tax charged by our government on goods which are imported into the country. They are paid by whoever is doing the importing – meaning you if you order something like an e-bike directly from a company in China, or by companies like Amazon, Walmart, or Apple which import products from other countries by the shipload.

But in the end, the tariffs aren’t paid by China or Amazon or Apple. They are paid by you, the end consumer, because if their cost of goods increases, a retailer is of course going to raise their prices to continue to make a profit.

Industry observers note that tariffs also affect companies directly: if Home Depot wants to build a latest store or Chevron needs a new oil rig, the tariffs on imported steel, copper, lumber and a million other components will raise the cost of these construction projects. And they raise the cost of housing, because most of the building materials in houses come from multiple countries as well.

Industry observers note that on average, tariffs will result in higher prices for everything just like any other broad-based sales tax. And just like most other taxes, the overall effect is to slow the economy and reduce our spending power. On the positive side, all that tax money flows into the government’s pocket which could help fund the national budget and even reduce the deficit.

Sources indicate that of course, every government needs at least some tax revenue to function, so it makes sense to use some mix of sales, income and corporate taxes to get there. The most notable part is that the levels need to be as low as possible while still keeping the country running well, and as fair and predictable as possible, so that people and businesses have an incentive to work hard and the ability to proposal far into the future.

And that’s where our current tariff regime gets it completely backwards. Donald Trump is throwing around random, extremely high tariff numbers as threats, then walking them back and changing them on an almost daily basis..

Whoa, that Sounds Mostly Bad – Is There a Good Side of Tariffs?

According to recent reports, sometimes, a country will use tariffs to protect their own domestic industries. For example, if you put a tax on imported Hondas, then General Motors cars will gain a competitive advantage – so GM will make more money. In this example, most consumers end up losing due to increased prices and decreased selection. But at least domestic auto manufacturers and their employees are happy.

This can be strategic (for example we might want to slap a tax on imported fighter jets to make sure Boeing and Lockheed can remain in business, for national defense purposes.) Or it can be corrupt (a politician might receive funding from kingpins in the steel industry, and in return then push through tariffs on imported steel to protect the profits of US steelmakers.).

Sources indicate that and this isn’t just a Trump or Republican thing either – Joe Biden used tariffs during his terms in an attempt to please swing-state voters. One of the worst examples was a tax on imported solar panel components (which Trump has since raised even further, proving that Boneheadedness can be Bipartisan). These are sheets of cheap glass that literally pump the cheapest energy and easiest wealth into your country for 30 years as soon as you plug them in. Cheap energy lowers everyone’s cost of living while also boosting industry. There is no good reason to block such wealth from flowing across your borders.

Can Tariffs Bring Us More Jobs?

In a recent development, let’s go back to that hypothetical tax on Hondas, and let’s say it’s a substantial one like $5000. At that level, many buyers will start heading over to the GM dealer next door to consider what he’s selling. Sure, the GM cars may not be as good, but for five grand some people are going to settle in order to save some money.

Because of this, GM’s sales go up. So they hire more employees and build more factories. They might even develop some new models and new technologies in response to all that new demand. More people learn advanced skills and in the best case it becomes a virtuous circle.

Sources indicate that but in exchange for this boom in the auto industry, everyone else has to pay more for slightly shittier cars and trucks. Higher vehicle prices means Amazon will have to spend more on their delivery fleet, so they will raise prices slightly on everything they sell. Somewhere a startup company or a medical breakthrough will be just a bit less likely to happen, because they are operating in an environment that is just a bit more expensive and a bit less efficient.

In a recent development, on top of that, with GM liberated from the hassle of competing with Honda, it will have less incentive to innovate and streamline itself. So its overall trajectory will be slower and less efficient even if its profits are higher.

Recent findings suggest that this big picture effect is why most economists agree that tariffs should be used very sparingly. They almost always cause unexpected damage, decrease overall employment and slow down an economy, but sometimes (like for food security or national defense) those costs are worth paying.

So Why is Donald Trump Throwing Around Tariffs Like They Are The Best Thing Ever?

This has been confusing to almost everyone. If you take him at his word, he appears to have a Bizarro Opposite Universe belief system about economics. Donald has claimed in speeches that the tariffs will somehow make us wealthier. He’s focusing on the first-order effects like GM hiring more workers, while completely ignoring the fact that everything else in the country gets less efficient in exchange.

But when he confirms larger tariffs, share prices go down, because everyone who actually runs or invests in US companies knows that of course they will make less money on average. When tariffs are paused or reduced, share prices go back up. Yet he keeps wielding the threats and we go back and forth.

It seems to be obvious to everyone except Donald himself that Tariffs are just a national sales tax rather than some clever sneaky strategic weapon, which leads to various theories that okay, maybe he knows that too but is just pretending in order to gain some influence.

The basic theory goes like this:.

Industry observers note that so right now our entire economy is subject to the whims of a single person.. And as long as this is the case, we’re just the same as any other dictatorship – something our constitution was supposed to prevent with the whole “three independent branches of government” thing.

It has been revealed that but presidents have tried to break out of their constitutional cage and get more power many times in the past, and this is just the latest example. The real test will be if our system eventually manages to stop this abuse and put itself back in balance as it always has in the past. You can already see this fight beginning to play out in our court system, in this Economist article:.

How Big are the Tariffs Right Now?

Even without the 145% nonsense numbers that were thrown around a few months ago, they are still far higher than they have been in the last 75 years or more. While it would be hard to pin down the current numbers in a stationary blog post like this one, the key thing to remember is that our current US economy is built around very low tariffs and relatively free trade.

Why haven’t I noticed Prices Going Up Yet?

While the US economy is fueled by a constant stream of cargo ships, as a whole we function like the biggest cargo ship of all: we have a huge inventory and it takes a while to change directions.

So in normal times, we already have several months of inventory of most things in the country. And then when all this drama started, importers started placing even more orders to stockpile things in advance before the tariffs hit. And now that they are in place, we’re importing a lot less stuff.

In a recent development, for now, we’re still using up the stockpiled inventory, but imports have dropped significantly so we’re quickly running out of cheap goods. If that happens, we will probably start seeing shortages and price increases throughout this summer or fall. For some things like plastic party trinkets, we can do just fine without. But if we lose access to core useful things like tools and machinery, the economic consequences will be much less fun.

The Dark Side and the Bright Side.

The most notable phrase to remember in US politics and economics is the phrase “This too shall pass.” The only mystery right now is that we don’t know exactly how it will pass. So we could sketch out a few scenarios:.

1) The current crazy-high tariffs really do stick around:.

I personally think this is the less likely scenario because nobody really wants it. But just as a thought experiment, it might go something like this:.

2) They do end up being just a negotiating tactic and we go back to mostly low tariffs.

In other words, the best way to win the tariff game is not to play it.

It has been revealed that just as much of US prosperity is built upon our huge population of 330 million people living in 50 states with open borders and no trade restrictions, all (friendly) countries of the world can benefit from the free exchange of goods, services and even people. We’re all human beings and if we treat each other with a collaborative respect, we all grow richer.

Epilogue: Is it Almost Over Already?

According to recent reports, I started writing this article on April 2nd, when Donald announced his “Liberation Day” and the stock market reacted with the biggest drop since 1932. Some people panicked and locked in big losses despite decades of warnings from your favorite financial bloggers, like this unfortunate soul in the comments to a JL Collins post:.

But as I watched over the next two months, we have bounced our way back up – with each drop in proposed tariffs triggering a corresponding increase in stock prices (a measure of investor enthusiasm of how bright our future looks).

According to recent reports, right now, the US stock market is just about back to its all-time high. This doesn’t match with our current level of tariffs, which are still about seven times higher than they were before the circus opened. But it shows that investors believe it’s all going to end with a truce and a resumption of free-ish international trade.

It has been revealed that if they’re wrong, the roller coaster ride will still have some more fun in store for us. But as long as we eventually end our current experiment in “emergency” tariff dictatorship and get back to functioning as a democracy, things should be just fine in the long run. I’m still 100% invested myself, so that’s where I place my bet.

The Biggest Lesson: Don’t Form Your Opinions Based on News Headlines.

Recent findings suggest that decades ago in a brighter age of journalism, there may have been a time when headlines were designed primarily to inform us, with just a bit of sizzle and spice to pull in our attention. Unfortunately, nowadays the priorities have flipped where the primary goal is attention, and accuracy carries little or no weight. Even a totally inaccurate article makes money for the publisher.

So while Democrats and Republicans like to do battle over which media sources are biased, in reality they’re all wrong: all click-funded commercial media is biased – sometimes politically but even more importantly biased towards generating outrage and fear, because those generate more money.

There are two solutions to this:.

1) Either ignore the media completely and focus on your own life, or.

2) Become a subject matter expert on things you really care about, and then read the original sources whenever you want to learn about something.

Industry observers note that I mostly practice option #1, but as a science and technology nerd I get into #2 in just the areas I find most interesting. And it’s amazing how the more deeply you understand a subject, the more you see just how wrong most media stories are about your area of expertise. Which means they’re probably pretty wrong about almost everything.

In a recent development, so as always, with this lesson learned it’s time to shut down that phone and laptop, exhale all our worries and get back outside with your real-life family and friends. See you in a few months!

    #148303. Breaking: Gifting Your House Costs Your Family the Tax Break They’d Get by Inheriting It

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (379 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Moneycrashers ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: Gifting Your House Costs Your Family the Tax Break They’d Get by Inheriting It

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (379 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Moneycrashers

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Giving your house to a child or grandchild while you’re alive hands them your cost basis, the figure their capital gain is measured from, so selling it can cost them tax on years of growth.
    • Signing the house over to family looks simple, until they sell.
    • According to recent reports, your cost basis is what you paid for the house plus improvements.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Giving your house to a child or grandchild while you’re alive hands them your cost basis, the figure their capital gain is measured from, so selling it can cost them tax on years of growth. If its value has climbed, leave it to them instead, since an heir who sells owes tax only on growth after your death.

    Signing the house over to family looks simple, until they sell.

    According to recent reports, your cost basis is what you paid for the house plus improvements. Say a mother paid $90,000 for her house and gives it to her son, who sells it at today’s $490,000 value. He takes her $90,000 basis, so the sale leaves him a $400,000 taxable gain. If he owns and lives in it two of the five years before selling, the home sale tax exclusion shelters up to $250,000 of it ($500,000 on a joint return). She’d also file a gift tax return, but owe gift tax only after using up a lifetime exemption in the millions.

    If he inherits it at that value instead, his basis steps up to $490,000, and he owes nothing on the sale.

    Sources indicate that so if your house has gained value, leave it at your death through a will, a living trust you can change, or a transfer-on-death deed where your state allows one. If it must change hands sooner, sell it at market value, lending the buyer the money through seller financing if needed, so their basis is the price paid. Or give only part of it, and the share you keep steps up at your death.

    A gift during your life carries other costs too:.

    Before anyone signs a deed, have an estate planning attorney in your state draw it up.

    Industry News: Interest-Free Credit From Suppliers – Ask for Longer Terms and Pay on the Due Date

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (506 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Moneycrashers

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that supplier payment terms are credit that charges no interest, and every extra day you get keeps cash in your business.
    • Sources indicate that paying suppliers on delivery, or paying each invoice the day it arrives, hands over cash that terms would let you keep for weeks.
    • Sources indicate that terms like net 30 give you 30 days after the invoice date to pay the full bill, with no interest.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that supplier payment terms are credit that charges no interest, and every extra day you get keeps cash in your business. Once you’ve paid a supplier on time for a few months, ask for 30 to 60 days to pay. Then pay each bill on its due date, not early, unless the supplier offers a discount for paying sooner.

    Sources indicate that paying suppliers on delivery, or paying each invoice the day it arrives, hands over cash that terms would let you keep for weeks. That cash could be covering payroll, rent, or the next order.

    Sources indicate that terms like net 30 give you 30 days after the invoice date to pay the full bill, with no interest. Take a gift shop that buys about $12,000 a month from its two biggest suppliers and pays on delivery. Moving both to net 45 means it pays for each order a month and a half later, so about $18,000 more stays in its account going into the holiday season.

    Ask for longer terms after a few months of paying a supplier on time, since that record is your best argument. Go from paying on delivery to net 30, or from net 30 to net 45 or net 60. Better still, ask for terms that match how long your own customers take to pay you, so their payments come in by the time your bills come due.

    It has been revealed that then pay on the due date, not before and never after, with each payment scheduled in your bank’s bill pay to arrive that day. Many suppliers report how you pay to Dun & Bradstreet, whose PAYDEX business credit score tracks how promptly you pay them. A late payment can pull that score down, and it gives a supplier reason to shorten your terms, not lengthen them.

    According to recent reports, the exception is a discount for paying early. Terms of 2/10 net 30 take 2% off a bill paid within 10 days and otherwise give you 30 days to pay it in full. Saving 2% for paying 20 days sooner is like earning about 37% a year on that money, far more than a savings account pays, so take the discount whenever you have the cash to spare. Offering your own customers an early-payment discount turns that 37% into a cost you pay.

    Start with the supplier you pay the most, since every extra 30 days of terms keeps about one month’s worth of its bills in your account.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that if you can afford a loved one’s bail, pay it in full to the court.
    • Say a judge sets $5,000 bail, the charges are later dismissed, and the court deducts nothing.
    • The court holds the cash until the case is over, which can take months, and some courts keep part of it.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that if you can afford a loved one’s bail, pay it in full to the court. The money comes back when the case ends, as long as they make every court date, minus any fees or fines the court deducts. A bail bondsman’s fee, usually 10% of the bail, is gone even if the charges are dropped.

    Say a judge sets $5,000 bail, the charges are later dismissed, and the court deducts nothing. A mother who paid her son’s bail in cash gets all $5,000 back, while a neighbor who paid a bondsman the usual 10% fee on the same amount is out $500 for good.

    The court holds the cash until the case is over, which can take months, and some courts keep part of it. New York keeps 3% of it after a conviction, and Florida first withholds any unpaid court costs and fines the defendant owes. Even that 3% is less than a third of a bondsman’s usual 10% fee.

    A bondsman gives the court a written promise to pay the full bail if the defendant misses court, and the fee pays for that promise. Whoever pays the fee usually signs as the cosigner, on the hook for that full amount, so the fee isn’t the most you can lose. The bondsman may also hold collateral against that debt, such as your car’s title or a lien on your house.

    Recent findings suggest that illinois, Kentucky, Oregon, and Wisconsin ban bail bondsmen, and Illinois ended cash bail entirely in 2023. Wherever a judge sets bail, take these steps:.

    Whichever you choose, put every court date on your calendar and get the defendant to each one. One missed date can cost you the full bail.

    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Moneycrashers ↗ Open Full Page

    Renting to Section 8 Tenants Means Steady Rent – With Inspections, Rent Reviews & Paperwork

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (482 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Moneycrashers

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • With a Section 8 tenant, the local housing authority pays its share of the rent straight to you, but only for a unit that passes its inspection at a rent it approves.
    • HUD’s fact sheet for landlords promises timely payments and says voucher tenants stay in a unit seven to eight years on average.
    • The tenant usually pays 30% of their income after deductions toward rent and utilities, and the authority pays the rest, up to its payment standard, the most it pays for a unit that size.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    With a Section 8 tenant, the local housing authority pays its share of the rent straight to you, but only for a unit that passes its inspection at a rent it approves. Check your state and local law before you decide, since many states and cities bar turning down an applicant for paying with a voucher.

    HUD’s fact sheet for landlords promises timely payments and says voucher tenants stay in a unit seven to eight years on average.

    The tenant usually pays 30% of their income after deductions toward rent and utilities, and the authority pays the rest, up to its payment standard, the most it pays for a unit that size. The tenant pays any rent above the standard, but at move-in their share can’t top 40% of their income after deductions.

    Take a tenant with no deductions, in a unit whose rent includes utilities and falls within the standard. Earning $24,000 a year, they pay 30% of $2,000 a month, or $600, and on a $1,600 rent the authority sends you the other $1,000.

    In a recent development, before payments start, you sign a contract with the authority, add HUD’s tenancy addendum to your lease, and pass its inspection. A failed item means repairs and a recheck, often while the unit sits empty. Inspectors return at least every two years, or every three at a small rural authority. They use HUD’s Housing Quality Standards or the newer NSPIRE standard, which a July 2026 HUD notice tells every authority to adopt by Feb. 1, 2027.

    The authority also limits your rent to what similar unsubsidized units rent for. The addendum bars an increase during the lease’s first term and requires 60 days’ notice to the authority before a later one, which it checks against similar units too. So the program suits a unit that’s already in good repair and priced near local market rents.

    The authority’s payments depend on federal funding, which can run late. After the 2025 government shutdown, Georgia’s Department of Community Affairs didn’t pay landlords the rest of November’s housing assistance until Dec. 5. Under the addendum, you can’t charge the tenant the authority’s share or evict them over its late payment.

    The Poverty & Race Research Action Council lists the state and local laws that protect voucher holders. Where one covers your rental, screen voucher holders by the same written standard you use for every applicant.

    Spend your first day at a latest job meeting people, not hunting for documents. The night before, gather your bank details for direct deposit and the documents that prove you can work in the U.S. Once you’re there, ask your manager what success looks like in your first 90 days.

    In a recent development, you don’t have to pick your benefits on day one, but the window to enroll is often 30 days from your start. Missing it usually means waiting for open enrollment, which comes once a year at most employers. Find your deadline and put it on your calendar before you leave.

    #148295. Family or Friend Won’t Repay a Loan? Get a Payment Plan in Writing First

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (458 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Moneycrashers ↗ Open Full Page

    Family or Friend Won’t Repay a Loan? Get a Payment Plan in Writing First

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (458 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Moneycrashers

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that if a relative or friend has stopped repaying money you lent them, ask privately for a payment plan they can afford, with a set amount and start date.
    • Without a set payment or due date, repaying a loan is easy to put off, and every month of silence makes the subject harder to raise.
    • So skip the hints and make one specific request.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that if a relative or friend has stopped repaying money you lent them, ask privately for a payment plan they can afford, with a set amount and start date. Confirm it in a text they answer. Save a demand letter or small claims court for a broken plan, or forgive the rest and say so.

    Without a set payment or due date, repaying a loan is easy to put off, and every month of silence makes the subject harder to raise.

    So skip the hints and make one specific request. Call or meet in private. A text is easy to ignore, and with others listening, embarrassment can turn into an argument. Propose an amount and a schedule they can actually meet. A sister owed $2,400 might ask her brother for $100 a month starting next payday, which clears the debt in two years.

    Afterward, text them a short summary of the plan and ask them to confirm it. Their reply is a written record that they owe the money and agreed to repay it, which matters if the plan falls apart.

    Recent findings suggest that if payments don’t start, or start and then stop, put the request in writing. Send a short letter or email that states what they owe, the payments they missed, a deadline to pay, and that you’ll file in small claims court if they don’t. Keep a copy. California’s courts require you to ask for the money before you file, and your copy shows the judge you did.

    Once the deadline passes, file in small claims court. It takes claims up to a cap your state sets, from $2,500 in Kentucky to $25,000 in Delaware and Tennessee. Filing is cheap. California’s fee for a $2,400 claim is $50. For the hearing, bring the bank or payment app record of the transfer and every message in which they agreed to repay you.

    Suing a relative or friend can cost you the relationship, win or lose. When the relationship matters more than the money, forgive the rest on purpose and tell them it’s now a gift, which settles the debt for both of you. Then stop lending to that person. For anyone else, lend only money you could afford to give away.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that it all started last winter when I innocently posted a review for a heated vest I had bought on Amazon. I was happy with this fun fresh way to beat the winter and wanted to share it with others, so I gave it five stars. But soon after I clicked “Submit”, I got an email from Amazon which said something like,.

    Recent findings suggest that “Congratulations! You’ve been selected to join Amazon Vine for writing helpful reviews!”.

    I was already aware of Amazon Vine since I had seen product reviews from other people in the program – typically called “Vine Voices.” The basic idea of this program is that you can order stuff from Amazon for free, as long as you agree to review at least 80% of the things you order.

    “Hey, that’s cool”, I thought, “Who doesn’t like free stuff?

    Especially since I’ve already been writing product reviews out of the goodness of my heart – why not be rewarded for it?”.

    So without giving it much further thought, I clicked “accept” on their terms and conditions and joined the program.

    And so began a saga that has taken me on a surprising journey over the past nine months causing me to:.

    Okay, I’ll admit that there were also some upsides. My original idea was partly to save some money, by getting stuff I genuinely would have bought anyway, in a way that sounded fun. And that did happen – I saved at least a few thousand dollars on tools and materials for my construction business and the MMM-HQ Coworking space, for free. Plus, at least some of the motivation for signing up was to put myself through an experiment so I could write this blog article about it. And if you’re reading this, it looks like that happened too.

    But I was still surprised at how powerful the combination of small nudges and incentives from Amazon was able to hijack my frugality instincts –  and get me to do a bunch of work that wasn’t really the best use of my time.

    Sources indicate that so I figured if we review my journey and break it down with a bit of Behavioral Science, we could all learn a few valuable things by laughing at Mr. Money Mustache’s folly.

    Scarcity Brain and the Online Casino Effect.

    Sources indicate that one of the most interesting books I’ve read in recent years is Michael Easter’s Scarcity Brain. It’s an exploration of the sneaky ways that modern gambling platforms, marketing and social media algorithms are all built upon two weaknesses in our evolutionary programming:.

    As I look back now, I realize that I fell straight into those same traps, because the Vine program has all the key properties of a casino or a TikTok feed:.

    In a recent development, but occasionally, there will be genuinely useful things like super nice light fixtures, tools and plumbing parts, an EV charger, and even some clothing. My favorite ridiculous Eagle shirt as featured in the Mustachianism music video was an Amazon Vine find.

    As were a whole supply of super-realistic artificial plants, which while tacky in principle, have been amazing for hard-to-water courtyard garden areas at the MMM HQ.

    Recent findings suggest that I also had a lot of fun roping in friends and coworkers from HQ to help and share in the bounty. I let them help me request and review stuff that they wanted, and then they got to keep it. This seemed like a win/win because we shared the work and the fun of laughing at some of the ridiculous products available.

    Still, as I went through this experiment this spring and summer and allowed the system to coax me into doing 80 reviews so I could upgrade my account from Vine Silver to Vine Gold*, I noticed something didn’t feel quite right.

    According to recent reports, I was checking the Vine page every day for scores, even when I didn’t actually need anything. It would usually be a bust, but just often enough, something I actually wanted would come up, and I’d order it before it was too late. Scarcity and unpredictable rewards at work.

    In a recent development, then the bounty would come, I’d unpack it and photograph it with assembly-line speed so I could batch-write all the reviews once per week or so. For every review I did, I was spending time I’d rather spend doing something else. And for every questionable item I got, I was creating pollution and trash from its manufacturing and packaging – directly contradicting the main values of my life and my reason for writing this blog. And I saw all of this, yet I kept doing it!

    So Was This The Downfall of MMM?

    It has been revealed that during the worst of this consumerism bender, things were dire. I was getting packages almost every day and my recycling bin was overflowing with cardboard. My son and my girlfriend started laughing at some of my more frivolous purchases, so I found myself discreetly tucking away the boxes when they were around to evade scrutiny.

    But eventually, I moved into a recovery stage. I had been letting this habit continue out of laziness and as a form of procrastination: it’s very easy to order shit online and pretend I’m doing something useful, and much more difficult to get moving to do the things that really make my life enjoyable.

    But I’m old enough to know that hitting the running trails and the gym for my daily workouts, and making progress on all my construction projects, and focusing on the computer as a creative tool rather than an entertainment device so I can get stuff done like this blog post, are the things that bring me the most joy.

    According to recent reports, admittedly, some of the sucky factors of the Vine program helped make it easier to recover too. For every genuinely useful thing I found like a contractor-grade extension cord, I had to scan through endless screens of trinkets which not only wasted my time but actually pissed me off at their very existence.

    Recent findings suggest that I also noticed some of the deliberately reviewer-unfriendly features built into the program which reminded me that we reviewers are definitely just low-wage workers rather than any form of VIP. The search functionality is crap, and there is no way to filter or sort the results, because they want you to have to look through everything and they don’t care about the value of your time.

    In a recent development, then there is the hilariously bureaucratic AI-based evaluation system which would occasionally flag my totally tame, factual reviews as “Not meeting our Community Standards” without explaining what the problem was. So I’d have to go in and edit my review, randomly changing a couple of words and maybe some punctuation, and suddenly the AI would be pacified and accept my review. Just dumb.

    This is What “Fuck You Money” is For!

    Industry observers note that it dawned on me that for many people, this is just what “work” looks like. You are given a bunch of tasks and a bunch of rules to follow, in a system you didn’t create and don’t get much say in changing. And then as long as you crank out your TPS Reports without rocking the boat too much, you get your paycheck.

    It reminded me of the Uber Driving experiment I did way back in 2017: as soon as I started working as a driver, I could immediately see dozens of improvements that could be made to the system that would make it function better for both drivers and passengers. But since I wasn’t the boss, nobody wanted to hear my ideas.

    It has been revealed that experiences like these remind me that while I love hard work and I love learning new things every day, I greatly prefer being the boss. And I’ve gotten pretty damned accustomed to it after 20 years of financial independence, so I see no need to give it up.

    One interesting “gotcha” of the Vine program is that they do keep track of all the free stuff you get and send you a 1099 for its retail value at the end of the year. So it’s not really free, just discounted to whatever your marginal tax rate is (about 25% for me this year). If we peek into my account right now, this is how my 2025 is looking:.

    Sources indicate that so I got about $7000 worth of stuff, and could owe up to $1750 of tax on it. In my case, about 75% of it was “sold” to my business for commercial use (construction supplies which I used on jobs or HQ renovations) so it was effectively converted into real income rather than just tax burden. Some of it was stuff I would have bought anyway for my own house which I’ll gladly pay the taxes on. But there is also probably about $1000 of pure nonsense in there as well, for which I’ll owe a tax bill of $250 as penance for my itchy trigger finger on that “Order” button.

    It has been revealed that thanks to some advice from wise readers in the comments (below), I have since learned that in most cases you can mark down this estimated value by 80% before declaring it – because you have effectively eliminated most of the resale value by opening and reviewing the product. Thus my tax bill will be more like $50 rather than $250. More detail in this Reddit discussion here.

    According to recent reports, so here we are today. While I admit that I didn’t explicitly cancel my account, I used the “Keystone Habit” trick to override the temptation to view the Vine page – mapping that browser bookmark to my daily habits list instead, a little chart which I call my “Badassity Tracker”. The net result is that every time I click it, I’m taken straight to a reminder to get up from the computer and do a quick round of exercise, so I do that instead.

    Recent findings suggest that and of course my writing of this article may be a violation of the terms and conditions of the program (“the first rule of Vine is to not talk about Vine”), so it might even get canceled on me. (and if so I’ll let you know because that would be funny story as well).

    But I learned a lot about habits and addiction, and realized that this same feeling might be what drives people into One More Year Syndrome, as they keep working even when they can afford to quit. I have now coached enough people through this situation to see it is way more common than I would have ever guessed.

    As with all MMM articles, there’s a real life lesson in this story. It’s not really about Vine or me or my habits, it’s about you continuing to look at yourself and your life, and always questioning your own assumptions or patterns. And asking the people you trust most for feedback as well:.

    We will never be perfect, but the great news is we don’t have to be. All it takes is a little bit of self reflection and putting ourselves on a slightly better path, as often as we can as life goes on. We are all on a very long journey, so even a tiny course correction can make a huge difference in where we end up.

    Cash Is King for Small Businesses – Keep Three Months of Fixed Costs in Reserve

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (491 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Moneycrashers

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, keep a cash reserve worth at least three months of your business’s fixed costs, the bills that don’t shrink when sales do.
    • In 2025, the typical small business with a Chase business account had cash to cover less than 18 days of its usual spending if no money came in, the JPMorganChase Institute found.
    • Industry observers note that size the reserve by fixed costs, not total spending.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, keep a cash reserve worth at least three months of your business’s fixed costs, the bills that don’t shrink when sales do. Hold it in a separate business savings account that pays interest, so a slow season or a customer who pays late doesn’t force you into costly borrowing.

    In 2025, the typical small business with a Chase business account had cash to cover less than 18 days of its usual spending if no money came in, the JPMorganChase Institute found. With that little cash, one big customer paying a few weeks late can leave you short for payroll.

    Industry observers note that size the reserve by fixed costs, not total spending. When sales slow, you buy less inventory, but rent, insurance, loan payments, subscriptions, and the pay of the staff you keep come due in full. If your sales are seasonal, hold three months of those bills plus the part of them your slow-season sales don’t cover, since that gap returns every year.

    In a recent development, to build it, pick a share of a typical month’s profit and set up a recurring transfer of that amount into a separate business savings or money market account that pays interest. Kept out of checking, the reserve won’t get spent on everyday bills, and it stays apart from your household emergency fund, which covers your own bills if the business can’t pay you.

    Industry observers note that say a dental practice’s rent, staff pay, equipment loan payment, and insurance come to $45,000 a month. Its three-month reserve is $135,000, built over two years at $5,625 a month. When an insurer holds up the practice’s claim payments for six weeks, the practice covers payroll from the reserve instead of borrowing, then refills it as the payments arrive.

    Sources indicate that spend the reserve only on a real shortfall, such as a late payment, a slow season, or a broken machine you can’t work without, never on an opportunity like a bulk discount. Refill it from the next money that comes in, before you spend on anything that can wait. With a 13-week cash forecast, you can see a shortfall weeks before it hits. A business line of credit, opened while sales are strong, can cover a gap that outlasts the reserve.

    Pull last year’s bank statements, total the fixed costs, and divide by four for your three-month target. Then set up the recurring transfer before this month ends.

    The 101 money moves that matter most, from the foundations to protecting what you’ve built.

    #148287. Stepped-Up Basis – Heirs Owe No Tax on Past Gains if You Hold Your Winners

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (452 w)
    📖 Baca
    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Moneycrashers ↗ Open Full Page

    Stepped-Up Basis – Heirs Owe No Tax on Past Gains if You Hold Your Winners

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (452 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Moneycrashers

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that stocks, funds, and property you leave your heirs get a stepped-up basis, meaning each one’s cost for tax purposes becomes its value on the day you die.
    • Selling an investment that has grown for decades means paying tax on all that growth, and giving it to your children passes the taxable gain to them.
    • In a recent development, say a father bought shares for $20,000 that are worth $220,000 when he dies.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that stocks, funds, and property you leave your heirs get a stepped-up basis, meaning each one’s cost for tax purposes becomes its value on the day you die. The growth during your life then escapes capital gains tax. Hold your biggest winners rather than selling or giving them away, and sell your losers while you’re alive.

    Selling an investment that has grown for decades means paying tax on all that growth, and giving it to your children passes the taxable gain to them.

    In a recent development, say a father bought shares for $20,000 that are worth $220,000 when he dies. His daughter inherits them with a $220,000 basis, so if she sells them right away for $220,000, she owes no tax. Had he given her the shares a year earlier, she’d have taken on his $20,000 basis with them, and the same sale would leave her a $200,000 taxable gain.

    The step-up covers investments in taxable accounts, such as stocks and funds, plus real estate and other property. It doesn’t cover traditional IRAs and 401(k)s, whose withdrawals your heirs pay income tax on, just as you would. On property a married couple owns jointly, only the half that belonged to the spouse who died steps up, under IRS rules. In a community property state, where most of what spouses acquire while married belongs to both, the couple’s shared property usually steps up in full.

    So when you need money, spend cash or sell investments with little gain first, and keep your biggest winners. Sell losing investments while you’re alive, since the basis of an investment worth less than you paid drops to its lower value at death, and the loss you could have deducted is gone. With a house, leaving it to your children usually costs them less tax than gifting the house during your life.

    Bills to tax gains at death have come up in Congress, including the Equal Tax Act introduced in March 2026, but none has passed.

    Heirs should get each asset’s date-of-death value in writing, from the brokerage for investments and an appraiser for real estate, and keep it, since any later sale’s taxable gain is measured from it.

    #148285. Bank Error on Your Statement? Report It in Writing Within 60 Days

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (503 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Moneycrashers ↗ Open Full Page

    Bank Error on Your Statement? Report It in Writing Within 60 Days

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (503 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Moneycrashers

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that spot a debit card charge, transfer, or direct deposit on your bank statement that looks wrong?
    • It has been revealed that regulation E, the federal rule for electronic transfers, gives you 60 days from the statement to report an error, whether or not you’ve noticed.
    • In a recent development, A phone call counts as reporting the error and starts the bank’s 10 business days to investigate.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that spot a debit card charge, transfer, or direct deposit on your bank statement that looks wrong? Call the bank and follow up in writing within 60 days after it sent that statement. Federal rules then usually give it 10 business days to investigate, or longer if it credits your account while it does.

    It has been revealed that regulation E, the federal rule for electronic transfers, gives you 60 days from the statement to report an error, whether or not you’ve noticed. Read each statement the week it arrives, and turn on real-time alerts for large or unusual charges.

    In a recent development, A phone call counts as reporting the error and starts the bank’s 10 business days to investigate. The bank can require you to confirm in writing within 10 business days of your call. It must say so on the call and give you the address. Without that letter, the bank can leave the money out of your account until it decides.

    Paper checks fall outside Regulation E, and you usually have 30 days or less from the statement date to report a check error. Your account agreement sets your bank’s exact deadline. A wrong credit card charge follows a different law, with its own steps to dispute the charge. Report fraud the day you spot it, since what you can lose grows the longer you wait.

    Send the letter the day you call, and keep a copy. Give your name and account number, the transaction’s date and amount, and why it’s wrong. Say a $482 debit card charge shows up twice. You call and write 20 days after the statement, and the bank returns the $482 within a week.

    In a recent development, to take longer than 10 business days, the bank must credit your account for the disputed amount within them, though it can hold back up to $50 for a transfer it believes someone else made. It then has up to 45 days from your call, or 90 for a debit card purchase or a transfer started outside the U.S. For a transfer within 30 days of an account’s first deposit, the 10 business days become 20 and the limit is 90 days. A bank that finds no error must explain why in writing and, on request, send copies of the documents it relied on.

    If the bank finds no error and you disagree, file a complaint with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau and attach your letter and its explanation.

    In a recent development, hire one nanny together with another family, and each family usually pays about two-thirds of a nanny’s going rate while the nanny earns a third more. Put the nanny share’s terms in writing first, including how much notice a family gives before leaving, and pay the payroll taxes on your own share.

    Sources indicate that care.com’s 2026 Cost of Care Report puts the average cost of a nanny for one child at $870 for a 40-hour week, or $21.75 an hour. At two-thirds of that, each family in a share pays about $580 a week instead of $870, roughly $15,000 less over a year.

    The nanny comes out ahead too. Two families paying $14.50 an hour each give the nanny $29 an hour, a third more than the $21.75 one family pays, for watching both families’ children at once.

    According to recent reports, at about $580 a week, a share still costs more than a day care center, which averages $332 a week in the same report. The extra $248 a week buys care in a home with one other family’s children instead of a center’s classroom.

    Look for a family nearby that needs care during the same hours and has a child close in age to yours. Then ask what nannies near you charge one family, and set each family’s share at about two-thirds of that rate.

    Each family pays the nanny its share separately and counts as a household employer, so each owes Social Security and Medicare taxes once its pay for the year reaches the IRS threshold.

    Sources indicate that put the terms in writing before the first day, starting from the nanny share work agreement that Hand in Hand, a nonprofit network of household employers, publishes. Settle at least these:.

    It has been revealed that A family that quits the share leaves the other paying for a nanny of its own, $21.75 an hour at the national average instead of $14.50, until a latest family joins. Agree up front that a family leaving gives at least four weeks’ notice or keeps paying its share for four weeks.

    #148279. My Unexpected Journey to Hormone Replacement (TRT)

    📅 16 Dec 2025 • ⏱️ 14m • 📚 Deep Dive (2750 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Mrmoneymustache ↗ Open Full Page

    My Unexpected Journey to Hormone Replacement (TRT)

    📅 16 Dec 2025 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2750 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mrmoneymustache

    ⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • As a man of Science, I’m supposed to hide my enthusiasm about this somewhat controversial subject, and instead direct you only to the peer-reviewed studies.
    • But man, I feel like I’ve stumbled upon the fountain of youth here.
    • I’ve been interested in optimization and trying to get the most out of my body and mind since I was a little kid.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    As a man of Science, I’m supposed to hide my enthusiasm about this somewhat controversial subject, and instead direct you only to the peer-reviewed studies.

    But man, I feel like I’ve stumbled upon the fountain of youth here. And the more I dig into the details and the hype and controversy surrounding the field of Hormone Replacement therapy, the more I need to share the word about it to my fellow middle-aged people (both men and women).

    I’ve been interested in optimization and trying to get the most out of my body and mind since I was a little kid. I started vacuuming up all the training and nutrition books and magazines I could find while I was just a teenager, and that field still remains a favorite of mine over 30 years later. And if you’re a long-time reader here you’ve been reminded plenty of times of this interest, because health has always been the very heart of Mustachianism.

    It has been revealed that but a funny thing has been happening in the last ten years: even as I kept honing the healthy living habits and trying my best to improve, there seemed to be a force pulling me back almost as hard. So despite working a bit harder and smarter every year, I still felt myself riding a gradually declining tide of energy, motivation, and physical stamina.

    “Perhaps this is just what it means to grow old”, I thought to myself,.

    “But I’m still gonna keep fighting it!”.

    Yet there was one thing that didn’t quite fit. Why was I having this decline in energy, when some of my older friends weren’t? And why was I still seeing people out there in their 50s, 60s and well beyond doing things that I felt too tired to do today?

    One of these tireless friends is a guy named Kevin, who is the personification of the highly energetic successful middle-aged man. He’s a semi-retired serial entrepreneur (and extreme rock climber) who lives in Boulder. And through an interesting twist of fate, in April of 2025 he invited me out for a hike right around the time I was doing all this wondering. And during this hike (and climb) he told me about his latest venture, a boutique men’s health company that specializes in helping men just like us get their youth back through the process of testosterone replacement therapy.

    Recent findings suggest that long story short: his ideas planted a seed in my head, which led to a bunch of research and a growing interest in trying TRT myself. I had of course heard about the process, but for some reason never considered doing it until I heard Kevin’s enthusiasm: he had been on it for several years, and according to him it is a “night and day difference” in all the things you want in life: energy, focus, thinking speed, and of course physical health.

    In a recent development, another convenient twist of fate is that I happen to be dating an REI doctor – a Reproductive Endocrinologist and Infertility specialist who has two board certifications in exactly the relevant bodily systems that are affected by these hormones. And while she was initially skeptical that I needed more Testosterone (and in her practice she regularly sees the downsides of men taking the stuff too early in life and thus compromising their own fertility), she has followed along and helped me learn at each step of this process, eventually becoming fully in support of the program.

    According to recent reports, so I signed up as a test customer for Kevin’s newly introduced manufacturer, which is called Bolt Health. I worked with their doctor to get a baseline blood test and review my numbers compared to all the past tests I’ve collected, and as it turned out, my levels had been dropping consistently over the years, and the latest test was by far the lowest ever.

    Even more telling, my age-related drop in Testosterone was correlating perfectly with my decline in energy and motivation:.

    Recent findings suggest that the next step was a prescription for a tiny daily dose of supplemental T, which arrived at my house the next week along with instructions for how to use it. And so began the journey.

    Now let’s jump forward seven months to the present day as I write this.

    Industry observers note that and wow, what a great year it has been! I only wish I had known and tried this a few years earlier, because I’m getting a lot more out of my life.

    Industry observers note that it’s not a night-and-day difference for me, but more like a 50% boost in overall youthfulness and energy. The biggest subjective change is that I just don’t have sucky tired days anymore, which was the main problem with my life before: wasting too much of my precious freedom due to not having the energy to enjoy it.

    This is why I’ve become somewhat of an evangelist for hormone replacement therapy for people from about age 45 onwards. It won’t work for everyone – if your levels are already pretty high, you don’t get the same boost. Two of my male friends tried TRT and quit because they didn’t notice any benefit. But these same two guys already had plenty of energy to begin with, which is usually a sign that the body has what it needs.

    It turns out I am very late to this party. Although Testosterone supplementation started out as a niche practice in the 1940s, from the 2010s onward it has been everywhere.

    TRT is the reason you see every actor suddenly showing up buff overnight for their superhero roles and it’s also why so many of today’s CEOs don’t look anything like yesterday’s CEOs.

    According to recent reports, in many cases, it has gone too far with young men using it just to gain muscle for the beach or the football field, and questionable online providers (aka “Prescription Mills”) handing out prescriptions to anyone with a valid credit card – with profit as their sole motive. It became overhyped in certain pockets of Bro Culture, where every Bro eventually receives the advice “Bro! You need to get on the T!” from another Bro, and therefore does it. And some of this reputation surely contributed to my own skepticism.

    According to recent reports, but there’s a lot of valid science behind TRT, if you’re the right candidate and you take the right dosage. And because of that, I feel it is probably under-hyped in my own demographic, the Nerdy Tech Worker Semi Retired Dad contingent. And that’s why I’m writing this blog post, because there are a lot of us out there.

    Many of us just tend to work with what we were given, and accept that aging means slowing down. And for those of us already enjoying an early retirement, we have the option of unlimited rest and recuperation time, so who really cares if we get tired a bit more often? After all, what better way to flex one’s wealth than with a decadent Tuesday Afternoon Nap while everyone else is stuck in the office?

    According to recent reports, while this seemingly healthy attitude has a lot of positive aspects, it can also mask a real problem which may be easily fixable. Because sometimes, the only thing that’s even better than an afternoon nap, is having the energy and motivation to go out for an afternoon hike, bike ride or adventure with friends. More energy is also pretty darned useful if you’re still raising kids or trying to do well in your career as a person over 45.

    How it Actually Works (and What Happened to Me).

    Industry observers note that distilling all of the fluffy discussion above into the simplest possible answer: TRT means using a tiny needle to inject a few drops of clear liquid just below the surface of your skin. And you do this by yourself at home, ideally once every morning.

    Here’s one of the baby needles I use for my daily dose.The typical serving is less than one tenth of a milliliter, which is only a few drops.

    According to recent reports, and while the term “needle” sounds scary to some, this is very different from the monstrosities they use to draw blood from your veins. This one is so miniature that you don’t need special training to use it, and you usually don’t even feel it.

    According to recent reports, so I began doing this to myself on May 1st of this year, while keeping a daily journal of my results along the way. The results seemed to be almost immediate in all the promised areas, but I know how powerful the Placebo Effect can be so I kept my skeptic’s hat on to see what would happen in the long run.

    I was seeing increased energy and motivation as well as lean weight gain through the whole spring and summer, but I remember the first truly shocking observation happened during a mountain vacation in July. I was part of a multi-family trip with lively adults, chaotic kids, early mornings, late nights with a few drinks, very intense high altitude sunshine and nonstop physical activities. It was just the type of situation that would drain my energy pretty promptly in the past.

    It has been revealed that but on day three I went out on a solo mountain bike ride to explore the area, and as I was climbing a long ascent with the blazing sun cooking me from every angle I just somehow kept having plenty of energy to keep climbing. Then I came down and joined the group for a few games of full-sun pickleball, biked back up the mountain to our cabin, and the story of unlimited energy went on from there.

    “Hot Damn”, I thought to myself, “I don’t know whose youthful and tireless body I have inherited here but I’d sure like to keep it!”.

    In August, the Bolt Health program scheduled a follow-up blood test for me and sure enough, my Testosterone levels had been boosted from 415 to 730ng/dL, bringing me from the low side of normal to the higher side.

    Many labs define “normal” as anywhere between 300 and 1000, which seems strange to me given the huge effect this hormone has on your wellbeing. It’s a bit like saying “Most cars have between 90 and 300 horsepower, so it doesn’t really matter what engine you have”.

    I mean yeah, either one will still get you down the road, but which one would you rather be driving?

    Sources indicate that since then, it has just been more of the same good results. My improvements ramped up and then just stayed there – so I’m operating at a new, much higher and more enjoyable level of functioning. Energy and motivation are no longer a problem, and I even find myself willing to make longer-term plans again (before this everything beyond same-day planning felt overwhelming). And my body seems to just want to gain strength and size with any excuse. Heavy weights feel lighter and the hard manual labor I still like to spend my time on feels easier for longer. It’s nice to be young again!

    So Why Doesn’t Everyone Do This?

    When you dig into the details, hormone replacement is mired in a soup of both real and incorrect information about both its benefits and its risks. And then our well-meaning medical establishment locks this whole container of soup deep in the cabinet with a label that indicates, “Needs Further Study”. But if you summarize the findings on both sides of the issue, you’ll see this:.

    Stuff you should do BEFORE trying TRT:.

    According to recent reports, the modern American Lifestyle is a Testosterone and Health Crusher. It’s a miracle that anybody feels good ever with the crap that people do to their bodies. So if you’re not already doing all the simple, natural, outdoor things that naturally boost your health, energy, and hormone levels, you’ll want to start with these first. You can find a pretty complete list on my oft-cited Badassity Tracker page.

    Recent findings suggest that since I was already doing all of these things pretty consistently, I felt ready to take the next step and at least consider hormone supplementation. But wait, there’s more!

    Many of the problems above are more likely to appear when the body is flooded with too much testosterone. In the bad old days, TRT was administered by sticking a pellet beneath your skin or injecting a large amount into the butt which then gets used up over the next several weeks. One friend recounted a story of extreme moodiness when the pellet was first implanted, ramping down to tiredness by the time the hormone was all gone.

    More modern providers like Bolt have fixed this problem by breaking the dose into much smaller servings which you administer each day. The idea is that your levels remain stable, and you need a lot less overall which reduces side effects.

    For my part, I have not had any of the negative side effects because I was a pretty ideal candidate in the first place: 50 years old with depressed Testosterone levels but an otherwise healthy lifestyle and no risk factors.

    Industry observers note that my hope in sharing this article is to be transparent and hopefully take some of the stigma out of this subject of other people who might benefit. Because in our modern over-connected world, everybody has an opinion on your life, even when you didn’t ask them.

    Industry observers note that and it’s not just men – many women in this same age group benefit from Estrogen replacement (and there are even interesting stories about female testosterone supplementation in certain situations as this author shares). The point is that aging is normal, but in some cases there’s a pretty easy way to make it slower.

    The great news is that Testosterone itself is a cheap and widely available substance, typically under $50 per month even for people like me without conventional insurance or drug coverage. The expensive part (here in the US) is just the doctor stuff – consultations, blood tests, ongoing analysis and prescription renewals and so on.

    The company that I used is positioned as a premium provider, bundling these services along with a bunch of other men’s health perks and deliveries for a few hundred dollars, which is expensive relative to most other parts of my budget, but still cheap if I consider the life and financial benefits of being 20-50% more energetic and productive.

    If you want to be on this program, your final decision will hinge on your income, insurance coverage if applicable, whether your existing doctor can already help you, and how much service and advice you’re willing to pay for.

    Recent findings suggest that note: I decided not to become a Bolt health affiliate because I wanted to write this article without conflict of interest. And I can honestly say, Bolt’s product and service seem great to me because I know and trust the people who run it. But  it’s also the only one I’ve tried. So I don’t know much about the competition and there may be other good options out there. At the very minimum, you can always try one service and switch to another if you don’t like the first one.

    According to recent reports, I’ve got lots more to say on money and early retirement, and lots of interesting projects in the works now too. So I’m thankful to have stumbled upon this booster for all aspects of life, so I can do more of everything else, for even more decades than I had expected.

    I wish this same type of good fortune for you, however you create it.

    According to recent reports, in the Comments: Do you have questions about hormone replacement or anything else in this article? I’ll try to invite Kevin, Dr. Sean Bender and other knowledgeable people to contribute and answer questions as well.

    #148275. Pay 0% Tax on Long-Term Gains – Sell and Rebuy in a Low-Income Year

    Pay 0% Tax on Long-Term Gains – Sell and Rebuy in a Low-Income Year

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (505 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Moneycrashers

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, in a low-income year, like early retirement or a gap between jobs, you can sell investments held over a year free of federal tax while your taxable income, gains included, stays in the 0% bracket.
    • This year the IRS puts the top of the 0% bracket for long-term gains, on investments held more than a year, at $98,900 of taxable income for a married couple filing jointly and $49,450 for a single filer.
    • Taxable income is income after deductions.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, in a low-income year, like early retirement or a gap between jobs, you can sell investments held over a year free of federal tax while your taxable income, gains included, stays in the 0% bracket. Sell up to the bracket’s top and buy back what you want to keep, so a later sale is taxed only on newer gains.

    This year the IRS puts the top of the 0% bracket for long-term gains, on investments held more than a year, at $98,900 of taxable income for a married couple filing jointly and $49,450 for a single filer. They rise to $102,100 and $51,050 in 2027.

    Taxable income is income after deductions. Your room is the top minus the rest of the year’s taxable income, dividends included. Only the profit counts, not the whole sale price, and profit past the top is taxed at the next rate, 15%.

    Industry observers note that A married couple who retire at 60 with $40,000 of taxable income can sell long-held funds at a $50,000 gain and owe no federal tax on it. On a Marketplace health strategy, though, the gain counts as income for the premium tax credit that lowers their premiums. Since 2026, the IRS allows no credit when household income tops 400% of the poverty line, and any advance payments must be repaid.

    Sources indicate that the 0% rate is federal, so your state may still tax the gain. If you collect Social Security, the gain can make more of your benefits taxable, and each newly taxable dollar shrinks your room by a dollar.

    The wash sale rule only blocks deducting a loss when you rebuy within 30 days. So you can buy the shares back the same day and still take the gain at 0%, unless your mutual fund limits quick buybacks. The rebuy resets your cost basis, the figure future gains are measured from, to today’s price. The upcoming shares need more than a year to qualify for the long-term rate again.

    Parents can pass this break to a grown child just starting out by giving appreciated shares, which keep your cost basis and the time you’ve held them.

    According to recent reports, first settle what you’ll take from traditional IRAs or move into a Roth, since both are taxable income that fills the room before gains do. Then sell in December, once the year’s income is clear. The trade date decides which year’s return the gain goes on, so place the sale by the year’s last trading day.

    The 101 money moves that matter most, from the foundations to protecting what you’ve built.

    Latest Update: Store Card Discount at Checkout – Pay in Full and You Keep All of It

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (541 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Moneycrashers

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that pay a store card’s balance in full by the first due date, and its checkout discount is yours to keep.
    • In a recent development, say the clerk offers 15% off a $600 TV if you open the store’s card today.
    • Industry observers note that that leaves you about $3 ahead of paying $600 up front.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that pay a store card’s balance in full by the first due date, and its checkout discount is yours to keep. If you’d carry the purchase instead, a year of interest at the card’s rate, often above 30%, can cost as much as the discount saves. That’s still cheaper than carrying it on a typical credit card.

    In a recent development, say the clerk offers 15% off a $600 TV if you open the store’s card today. That’s $90 off. But pay off the remaining $510 in 12 equal monthly payments at a 30% annual percentage rate (APR), and by our math the interest comes to about $87.

    Industry observers note that that leaves you about $3 ahead of paying $600 up front. If you’d carry the TV either way, the store card is still cheaper than a general-purpose card, at the cost of a hard inquiry on your credit report. Those averaged a 25% APR in 2024, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) found. By our math, 12 payments on $600 at that rate cost about $84 in interest, so the store card comes out about $88 ahead. Store-only cards averaged 31%, and many charge every cardholder the same rate, so strong credit won’t get you a lower one.

    In a recent development, FICO says a hard inquiry takes less than five points off most people’s scores and stops counting after a year. If your credit is strong, a store-only card’s starting limit is typically less than half what a general-purpose card would give you, the CFPB found. So the same $510 balance takes up a bigger share of the limit. That raises your credit utilization, which can lower your score until you pay it down.

    After the first purchase, the card is worth using only if you shop there constantly and pay it in full every month. If you shop there only now and then, a no-annual-fee card that earns 2% back on everything you buy is the better everyday card. For the store’s rewards, ask whether it also offers a co-branded card, which many massive retailers do. It carries the store’s name but works at other stores too.

    Financing that’s interest-free only if you pay in full by a deadline is deferred interest, a different deal with risks of its own.

    Take the discount only on something you came to buy, and pay the card off before you charge anything else to it.
